standing: No legal standing: the 1973 Constitution's equality clause does not list language
It is named in a curriculum, the Grade 1 Primary Language Arts Curriculum 2022-2027
Objective 1.6 gives it seven weeks of the Grade 1 speaking and listening strand
What it obliges is teaching pupils to use Standard English and dialect appropriately
mediumOfInstruction: Not a medium: Standard English is for the classroom, dialect for casual settings
At Grade 1 pupils hear a dialect phrase and render it in Standard English
The document is the national Grade 1 Primary Language Arts Curriculum 2022-2027
Set by a curriculum objective, a teaching expectation rather than an entitlement

sources.label: UNESCO GEM Report PEER, Bahamas: Inclusion profile (archived platform)
Ministry of Education (Bahamas), Grade 1 Primary Language Arts Curriculum 2022-2027 (web.archive.org mirror of 4 February 2023; the live curriculumbahamas.com url now returns HTTP 404)

standing: Arabic alone: Basic Law art. 1 gives the Kingdom one language and names no other
The instrument is the 1992 Basic Law of Governance, in its 2013 revision
UNESCO's profile records a vote for UNDRIP and no recognition of any other language
Art. 29 binds the State to preserve Arab and Islamic heritage; it names no language

sources.label: Basic Law of Governance of Saudi Arabia, 1992 (rev. 2013), arts. 1 and 29 - Constitute Project English text
UNESCO GEM Report PEER, Saudi Arabia: Inclusion profile, section 'Linguistic and ethnic groups'

standing: No minority standing: San Marino reports it has no ethnic minorities on its territory
Said in a state report under FCNM art. 25(1), not in any San Marino instrument
Its recognition of national minorities is called only a hypothetical commitment

sources.label: Second report submitted by San Marino under art. 25(1) of the Framework Convention for the Protection of National Minorities, ACFC/SR/II(2004)013, received 23 August 2004 (rm.coe.int refuses a bare curl and serves the document to a browser user-agent)

standing: Latin is the Church's own language: the Roman Pontiffs adopted it as such
Fixed by the motu proprio Latina Lingua, given at St Peter's on 10 November 2012
The Academy it sets up has its headquarters in Vatican City State
The most solemn official Acts of the Roman Pontiffs are authentic in Latin

sources.label: Benedict XVI, Apostolic Letter issued motu proprio Latina Lingua establishing the Pontifical Academy for Latin, 10 November 2012, with its annexed Statutes
